qa.q: Is Black Friday too late to buy an advent calendar?
qa.a: It is the last comfortable week. A 24-day calendar starts on December 1, and Black Friday 2026 falls on November 27, so an order placed that day has four days to arrive. A 12-day calendar that ends on Christmas Eve starts on December 13 and leaves more room. Check the delivery date on the retailer page before you pay, since this page shows prices and not shipping times.

qa.q: Do advent calendars get cheaper after December 1?
qa.a: Often, but the choice shrinks first. Once the countdown has started, sellers cut what is left, and the calendars that sell best are gone by then. If the calendar is a gift that has to be opened on day one, the price on the check date above is the one that counts. A calendar bought late still works: open the missed doors on the first evening.

qa.q: How do I know an advent calendar discount is real?
qa.a: Look at the final price and the cost per day, not the percentage. A list price is set by the seller, and this table shows it only so you can see the gap the retailer reports. Divide the price by the number in the Days column and compare calendars of the same kind: our guides for each kind do that sum for every calendar they list.

qa.q: What kind of advent calendar can you get under $25?
qa.a: Most are chocolate and candy calendars, crystal and jewelry sets, nativity and paper picture calendars and small beauty sets. Paper picture calendars with 24 doors sit at the low end of the table. The Kind column shows which is which.

qa.q: Is a cheaper advent calendar worse value?
qa.a: Price alone does not say. Divide the price by the number of days: a calendar with 24 doors costs half as much per day as a 12-day one at the same price. What a day holds matters more than the total, and the product page of each calendar lists that from the maker listing.
